skill.name: gh-address-comments
skill.description: Organize and address review comments on the current branch's open GitHub pull request through the gh CLI.
skill.summary: Summarize GitHub PR feedback and apply only the fixes selected by the user.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Three backtick detections are Markdown code spans, and the fixed date substitution has no injection path. The hook performs a persistent hidden-home write after every Bash command, while the instructions request unnecessary workflow scope and broad elevation. Publication should wait until logging and privilege requests are narrowed.

remediation.issue: A broad PostToolUse hook appends to a hidden file after every Bash command.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the hook, or use a user-approved project log restricted to relevant gh operations with size controls.

remediation.issue: The instructions request workflow scope and blanket elevated access for gh commands.
remediation.suggestion: Request only the minimum GitHub scopes and elevate individual commands only after explicit user approval.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 uses Markdown backticks to format the gh command name. It does not contain Ruby or shell execution syntax.
Line 18 uses Markdown code spans for example gh commands and a permission value. The backticks do not execute those strings.
Line 31 formats gh auth login as inline Markdown. No Ruby or shell backtick expression is present.
The hook substitutes only the fixed date command into a constant log message. No user-controlled input reaches the shell substitution.
The PostToolUse hook appends to ~/.claude/gh-address-comments.log after every Bash action. This creates persistent, unbounded hidden state outside the project.
Line 11 writes to a hidden path under the user's home directory through shell redirection. The broad Bash matcher triggers this side effect beyond gh commands.

content.value_statement: Review feedback can be difficult to organize and resolve. This skill summarizes open PR comments, asks which items to address, and guides selected fixes.
actual_capabilities: Checks gh CLI authentication before pull request operations.
Guides use of a referenced helper script to list comments and review threads.
Numbers feedback items and summarizes the change required for each item.
Asks the user which comments to address before editing files.
Applies focused fixes for the comments selected by the user.
Prompts for reauthentication when gh encounters authentication or rate issues.
limitations: The audited package does not include the referenced scripts/fetch_comments.py helper.
Requires a local gh CLI installation and an authenticated GitHub account.
Requests elevated network access and broader GitHub scopes than comment handling needs.
Does not define automatic replies, thread resolution, commits, or pull request updates.

use_cases.title: Triage Personal PR Feedback
use_cases.description: List and summarize feedback before choosing which requested changes to implement.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Maintainer Fixes
use_cases.description: Organize review threads and apply only the changes approved for the current maintenance cycle.

use_cases.title: Plan Team Review Work
use_cases.description: Turn scattered pull request comments into a numbered action list for assignment and discussion.

prompt_templates.title: List Review Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the open PR for my current branch, list review comments, and summarize each numbered item. Do not change files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Group Related Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect PR comments, group related feedback, and explain required changes. Ask which numbered items to address before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Selected Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Address comments [2, 4, 7]. Make focused edits, run relevant tests, and summarize changed files and unresolved feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Complex Review Resolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit all current PR threads. Propose an ordered resolution plan, identify conflicts, then implement only my approved items.

output_examples.input: List the review comments on my current pull request.
output: 1. Rename the validation helper for clarity.
2. Add a test for an empty response.
3. Explain the retry behavior in the documentation.

output_examples.input: Address comments 1 and 2, then summarize the result.
output: Renamed the validation helper and updated its references.
Added coverage for the empty response case.
Comment 3 remains unchanged because it was not selected.

best_practices: Review every numbered summary before approving file changes.
Grant only the GitHub scopes required for reading and updating the pull request.
Run relevant tests and inspect the final diff before responding to reviewers.
anti_patterns: Do not grant workflow scope solely to read or address review comments.
Do not modify feedback items that the user did not select.
Do not assume the referenced helper script exists without checking the installed package.

faq.question: Does this skill require the GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The gh CLI must be installed and authenticated before it can inspect the current pull request.

faq.question: Will it change every requested item automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks the user to select numbered comments before applying fixes.

faq.question: Can it find comments without an open pull request?
faq.answer: No. The workflow expects an open pull request for the current branch.

faq.question: Does the package include its comment-fetching script?
faq.answer: No. The audited package references scripts/fetch_comments.py, but that file is absent.

faq.question: Does it resolve GitHub review threads?
faq.answer: No automatic thread resolution is defined. It focuses on summarizing feedback and applying selected file changes.

faq.question: What permissions should I grant?
faq.answer: Use the minimum repository permissions needed for the pull request. Workflow scope is not required for comment handling.
